# Stack VM compilation strategies (Agent 1)

Retrospective ticket for compile-time partial evaluation of stacklang body
programs. Surface authoring language is unchanged; programs still use
`register_op(name, [literals, OpHandler tokens, ...])`.

## Strategy: tagged bytecode with early binding

At `run_op` time, `compile_body_to_wordbuf` lowers each authoring list into a
flat `WordBuf` of tag words plus resolved operands. The interpreter (`run_wordbuf`)
dispatches with a C `switch` on tags instead of walking Python lists or a
frame/PC loop.

## Strategy: operand resolution at compile time

- Native ops: `TAG_CALL_FN` + resolved `op_fn_t` pointer
- Nested bodies: `TAG_CALL_WB` + stable `WordBuf*` into `op_table`
- Literals: `TAG_LIT_INT` / `TAG_LIT_FLOAT` / `TAG_LIT_STR` / `TAG_LIT_OP`
- Primitives (`dup`, `f_add`, ...): dedicated inline tags (`TAG_DUP`, ...)

## Strategy: superinstruction fusion (peephole at compile)

Adjacent patterns fold into fewer instructions:

- `[lit, i_add]` -> `TAG_I_ADD_C`
- `[lit, f_add_at]` -> `TAG_F_ADD_AT_D` (float step-sum body becomes one insn)
- `[over, i_gt]` -> `TAG_OVER_I_GT`; with leading lit -> `TAG_I_GT_C_REV`
- `[whilefn, body, while]` -> `TAG_WHILE_BUFS` + two `WordBuf*` operands

## Strategy: `except -1` calling convention

`op_fn_t` returns `int` with `except -1`. Success is 0; errors propagate
without `PyErr_Occurred` polling in the dispatch hot loop. `pop_int` uses
`int64_t` end-to-end (no 32-bit truncation).

## Strategy: benchmark authoring (outside VM core)

`tests/stack_bench.py` bakes loop bounds at registration (`nextafter` for float
while, `stop+1` for int) so hot loops emit shorter bytecode. Ratchet test in
`test_stack_benchmark.py` requires `float_while` stacklang to beat Python.

## Files

- `imgcomp/_stack_c.pyx` (compile + tagged interpreter)
- `imgcomp/tests/test_stack_benchmark.py` (iter counts + ratchet)
